prompt.content: A hunk's context starts in the middle of a fenced code block. What would rendering the hunk lines as Markdown do?

choices.content: Treat the prose after the fence as code
Show the fence as plain text and nothing else
choices.explanation: A Markdown renderer has no way to know the fence started earlier; it reads the closing fence as an opening one.

choices.content: Fail to compile the lesson with an error
choices.explanation: Nothing checks Markdown validity; the fragment would render, just wrongly.

hints: What does a Markdown renderer do with a lone closing fence?
blocks.explanation: Without its opening line, the closing fence opens a new code block, so everything after it renders as code. Complete blocks from whole documents avoid that.

highlights.annotation: At depth 0, lists and block quotes become containers; every other block is one unit.
The direct children of a container, such as list items, are the units instead.
A top-level footnote definition adds its first through last source line to `definition_lines`.

prompt.content: A three-item list gains a fourth item. Which segments does the changed list produce?

choices.content: Three unchanged items and one added item
The list removed, then re-added whole
choices.explanation: Lists are containers, so each item is its own unit and the three old items match unchanged.

choices.content: One unchanged list with the new item inside it
choices.explanation: Segments are whole units; the new item is its own added unit, not part of an unchanged one.

hints: What are the units inside a top-level list?
blocks.explanation: Each item of a top-level list is a unit, so matching finds the three existing items unchanged and only the new item added.

highlights.annotation: Take one removal and one addition at a time, so each old block sits next to its replacement.
An unchanged block ends a run of changes: flush it before keeping the block.

prompt.content: A heading and the paragraph below it both change. In what order do the four segments appear?

choices.content: Old heading, new heading, old paragraph, new paragraph
Old heading, old paragraph, new heading, new paragraph
choices.explanation: That is the raw subsequence order; `pair_replacements` interleaves it.

choices.content: New heading and new paragraph only, marked as changed
choices.explanation: Removed blocks are kept and shown struck through, so the reader sees what was replaced.

hints: What does `flush` take from each list on every turn?
blocks.explanation: Within a run of changes, `flush` takes one removal and one addition at a time, so each block's old and new versions sit next to each other.

highlights.annotation: An unchanged block survives only if it overlaps a displayed old or new line; removed and added blocks below follow the same rule.
Hidden steps are counted and emitted as one gap before the next visible segment.

prompt.content: A 40-block document changes one paragraph in the middle, with `context_lines` 1. What does the rendered view show?

choices.content: A gap, the changed paragraph, then another gap
All 40 blocks, with the paragraph marked
choices.explanation: The rendered view covers the same region as the line diff, not the whole document.

choices.content: Only the changed paragraph, with no gaps
choices.explanation: Leading and trailing blocks outside the hunks are summarized as gaps so the reader knows more exists.

hints: Which blocks overlap a displayed line when only one line of context is shown?
blocks.explanation: Only the blocks overlapping the hunk's lines are kept; the blocks before and after collapse into one gap each.

highlights.annotation: Only files whose language resolves to Markdown are read in full.
Before: the base blob; a new file has none.
After: the target blob for a revision, otherwise the worktree file; a deleted file has none.
The two documents and the hunks become the frozen segments.

prompt.content: An agent diffs `docs/SETUP.md` with an inline patch. What does the learner see?

choices.content: The line diff, and lint reports an info finding
The rendered view, built from the patch hunks
choices.explanation: Hunks are fragments; only Git sources give the complete documents needed for rendering.

choices.content: An error, because lint rejects Markdown patches
choices.explanation: The rule is `info`: a hand-made patch is sometimes the only option.

hints: Which diff source gives the compiler both complete documents?
blocks.explanation: Only `git` sources get `rendered`, so an inline patch keeps the line view, and `lint.diff.markdown_patch` suggests a `git` source.

highlights.annotation: A gap only reports how many blocks were left out.
Every other segment is a complete block rendered by the normal Markdown component, with a hidden label for changes.
